attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to run a Kea DHCPv4 server on the shared 10.100.56.0/24 network with static reservations for node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 (RHEL7) to obtain their address from node1 rather than the platform's own DHCP responder. Since all three nodes share a single flat egress network where the platform gateway (10.100.56.1) also runs an active DHCP server, a `reject 10.100.56.1;` directive was added to dhclient config on node2/node3 so they deterministically source their lease from node1 instead of racing with the platform. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs changed on each, and post-reboot state confirms node1's DHCP server auto-started and node2/node3 re-acquired their addresses (10.100.56.11/.12) via DHCPACK from node1 (10.100.56.10), preserving IPs and connectivity.
